intermediate.title: KOM Sprint (4) Côte de Billy-Chevannes (123.4 km)

story: A four-rider breakaway was kept firmly under control, never gaining more than two minutes as the peloton maintained a relentless pace. The escapees were caught with 6 kilometres remaining in what became the fastest stage in Tour de France history, averaging 50.91 km/h. Søren Wærenskjold launched a long-range sprint to beat Olav Kooij and Jasper Philipsen, whose third place was initially revoked before being reinstated following a jury review.
